column1: # Case corpus for the guards. One case per line: expectation TAB command.
# `deny` means the guard must refuse it; `allow` means it must pass through.
# Run it with `hooks/guard-test.sh`. Run `hooks/guard-test.sh --mutate` to check the corpus
# still pins the guard: that run blanks one decision line at a time and reports
# any mutant the corpus fails to kill. Every case below marked with a mutant
# number was added because a surviving mutant showed nothing was holding it.
# A 100% mutation score proves this corpus pins the code that is here. It cannot
# find a check that is missing — those are found adversarially, and the cases
# --- 1a. secrets and machine config: no access at all -----------------------
# a redirect whose target basename is itself a reader: only the redirect check
# catches these, and nothing held it until a surviving mutant said so
# bypasses found adversarially in audit round 3
# false positives measured in audit round 3: reading and running are not writing
# readers that write nothing at all, refused until the list was widened (#4)
# the value of a wrapper flag is not the verb: this was judged on the word `root`
# gh talks to GitHub and git writes only under .git: system paths in their
# arguments are text, and the destructive git verbs are 3a's job

column2: gh issue create --body "the guard protects /System and /Library"
git commit -m "docs: cover /usr and /lib in the guard"

column1: # ~/Library is the user's own data, not a system tree
# git's global options sit where every pattern here reads the subcommand
# bypasses found adversarially in audit round 3: 3b was still an allowlist of
# destructive verbs, the design the deny-by-default rewrite ruled out for 1b.
# bypasses found adversarially against the round-3 version (#5). Each of the
# first three let every verb on the list through at once, which is worth more
# than any word added to it: a `git` at the head exempted the whole command,
# `segments()` cut inline interpreter code into pieces before it was read, and a
# wrapper flag's value was read as the verb.
# a second dash is still a flag that deletes
# the trash family, and coreutils under its Homebrew spelling

column2: gh pr create --title "chore: rm dead code"
git commit -m "fix: remove the old rm handler"
gh issue comment 1 --body "the rm path is denied"

column1: # a remote branch is git's to delete and 3a governs the destructive git verbs;
# an interpreter handed a file, not inline code, is running a script
# ~/Library is not one thing. Exempting the whole tree to fix a false positive
# opened its secret stores and its login-item directory in a single line.
